sections.label: DOORS AND MECHANISMS
sections.about: the gallery: the z-motion door family, a lift, a shot-open breach, and the E1M1 blueprints the owner attested
hand_composed: the gallery hall itself: a plain ashlar room, because no constructor owns a gallery

sections.label: FURNITURE HALL
sections.about: one hall of the furniture kinds the pipeline can place, each seated the way that thing is actually mounted
hand_composed: the hall itself; and the table volumes, which are raised sectors assembled here because templates.py's table lives on the levelprog stack and cannot be called from a PlanarLayout

sections.label: SHOP
sections.about: E6M1's shop re-expressed through our constructors: counter, shelf runs, crate stock and a display row
hand_composed: the shop room itself: worn facade tile 202 on the walls, which is a material choice and not a constructor

sections.label: STREET
sections.about: outdoor scale under sky: the frontage at two widths and the turnstiles that admit you to somewhere public
hand_composed: street anatomy: there is no kerb, no roadway and no gutter, because no constructor owns them and no owner anchor grades a road surface. The ground here is the gallery's own floor tile, which is the honest placeholder rather than a guess

sections.label: SEWER AND TECH
sections.about: a wet service passage: the sewer kit by the role each tile was mined under

sections.label: PARK
sections.about: outdoors under sky: the ground vocabulary and the things that grow in it

sections.label: TILE MUSEUM
sections.about: a gallery wall of the owner's anchor tiles, each lettered with the owner's own name for it
hand_composed: the panel bays: shallow sectors wearing one tile each, with no lighting of their own

exhibits.label: PUSH DOOR
exhibits.about: a z-motion door used from the room outside it
exhibits.try: press use on the door face; it should rise
exhibits.provenance: doors.z_motion_door(interaction='direct'). It sets Push AND Wallpush together and says why: a shut z-door has zero height, so the player stands in the hall and Wallpush is what fires
exhibits.expect_summary: 1 sector(s) of type 600, read as a changes what fits through, worked by a push

exhibits.label: SWITCHED DOOR
exhibits.about: the same motion, worked from a switch across the room
exhibits.try: press the switch on the side wall, not the door
exhibits.provenance: doors.z_motion_door(interaction='remote') and xsector_remote_rx; reports/blood-effects-switches.md
exhibits.expect_summary: 1 sector(s) of type 600, read as a changes what fits through, worked by a switch, listening on channel 300

exhibits.label: KEYED DOOR
exhibits.about: a door that wants the moon key, which lies in the room
exhibits.try: try the door, then take the key and try again
exhibits.provenance: doors.z_motion_door(key=6); E1M4 sector 295 wears the moon emblem; knowledge/blood/design/keys-v1.json
exhibits.expect_summary: 1 sector(s) of type 600, read as a changes what fits through, requiring key 6

exhibits.label: LIFT
exhibits.about: a floor that carries a body between two storeys, with a landing worth arriving at
exhibits.try: ride it up, step off, and look back down
exhibits.provenance: Vanilla/MACHINERY-LIFT.map s2, the basic exemplar of twenty-odd differing one field at a time; E1M3 sector 241, whose floor endpoints are exactly its neighbours'
hand_composed: the upper room that makes the ride worth taking
exhibits.expect_summary: 1 sector(s) of type 600, read as a carries a body between levels

exhibits.label: CRACK BARRIER
exhibits.about: a breach in a load-bearing wall, opened once by shooting it
exhibits.try: SHOOT the crack: it should blow, with three staggered puffs, and the breach opens once and stays open. It did nothing at all before -- it had been given a switch's wiring instead of a thing's
exhibits.provenance: E1M4 sectors 276 and 277, flush at rest; kThingWallCrack transmits once
hand_composed: the load-bearing wall the breach interrupts is plain masonry; no constructor owns a damaged-wall habitat
exhibits.expect_summary: 1 sector(s) of type 600, worked by a shot, listening on channel 301, one-way

exhibits.label: CASKET
exhibits.about: a lid that slides aside by MOVING THE BOUNDARY between hole and cover, over a room-over-room link, breathing light as it goes
exhibits.try: look up, then walk out; E1M1 opens inside one
exhibits.provenance: owner-attested E1M1 reading, sectors 28/30 (hole, slide-marked, ROR-linked) and 27/29 (cover). Each slide sector moves exactly ONE flagged wall, and that wall is the hole/cover boundary
hand_composed: the SECOND pair: E1M1's casket is four sectors, and this is one pair plus its link. Building both, synced on one channel with the same travel on each side of the plane, is the next step
exhibits.expect_summary: 1 sector(s) of type 614, listening on channel 309, whose payload is 'boundary re-partition', stack-linked across a room-over-room plane

exhibits.label: DOUBLE SLIDE DOOR
exhibits.about: one sector, two leaves parting along their own line
exhibits.try: push it and watch where the leaves go
exhibits.provenance: owner-attested E1M1 sector 4; mechanism.sliding_gate built to the campaign template
exhibits.expect_summary: 1 sector(s) of type 614

exhibits.label: PLAIN SLIDE DOOR
exhibits.about: a single leaf sliding aside, the load-bearing kind
exhibits.try: open it and step through; nothing is dressed up
exhibits.provenance: owner-attested E1M1 sector 63. Its two portals are 512 apart on the SAME side, which is why the cheap blocking test almost never fires
exhibits.expect_summary: 1 sector(s) of type 614

exhibits.label: DOUBLE ROTATING DOOR
exhibits.about: two rotating leaves chained on one channel
exhibits.try: work one leaf; the other answers on the chain
exhibits.provenance: owner-attested E1M1 sectors 50 and 51: s50 transmits to s51, which is a sentence in the control-bus grammar, not two doors
exhibits.expect_summary: 2 sector(s) of type 615

exhibits.label: SHELF SECRET
exhibits.about: a BOOKCASE in a run of shelving that slides aside, and the secret room behind it
exhibits.try: press the switch on the masonry to the left of the shelving, then walk into the gap the bookcase leaves -- the room behind is the level's one secret and should be credited as you enter
exhibits.provenance: owner-attested E1M1 sector 70 (one sliding sector dressed as a bookcase); tiles 31/33 are owner anchors, 'bookcase front'; the secret credit is Vanilla/OTHERSECTORSFX-SECRETS.map s2 -- channel 2, kChannelSecretFound, with the NUMERIC command that carries the secret's index
exhibits.expect_summary: 1 sector(s) of type 614, listening on channel 304

exhibits.label: CURTAIN
exhibits.about: an internal FIN drawn across its own doorway -- the fabric stretching IS the animation
exhibits.try: push the CLOTH (not the frame) and watch the fabric gather: closed it hangs at natural scale, and opening squashes the texture hard, which is what cloth does
exhibits.provenance: owner anchor 146/147, binding strong, and the owner's note with them: a Blood curtain is a thin deforming sector, not a pair of leaves
exhibits.expect_summary: 1 sector(s) of type 614, listening on channel 303, whose payload is 'part of the sector travels', tiles 146 worn as wall texture, not thrown as sprites

exhibits.label: LIGHT FITTINGS
exhibits.about: the four light kinds, each on the surface it hangs from
exhibits.try: look up: the chandelier and lantern hang, the torch and sconce are on the wall
exhibits.provenance: furniture.py, whose mounting field is mined from the campaign: a torch is drawn fullbright in 89% of its 150 uses because it is on fire
exhibits.expect_summary: tiles 506/510/641/1701 placed as sprites

exhibits.label: WALL FITTINGS
exhibits.about: plaque, plank and ceiling plate: mounted things that are not lights
exhibits.try: the ceiling plate is floor-aligned and lies flat; it cannot hang on a wall and furniture.py refuses to try
exhibits.provenance: furniture.py mounting rules; the alignment state is a property of the tile, not of the caller
exhibits.expect_summary: tiles 68/795/915 placed as sprites

exhibits.label: TABLES
exhibits.about: tables as raised sector volumes at the campaign rise, not as sprites
exhibits.try: walk up to one: it is geometry, and you can stand on it
exhibits.provenance: projects/blood-city/level/templates.py TABLE_RISE = 0.30 player heights, TABLE_SIDE 1024

exhibits.label: GRAVEYARD
exhibits.about: the headstone and tomb set, seated on their own campaign heights
exhibits.try: check nothing floats and nothing is buried
exhibits.provenance: furniture.py graveyard entries; every height is the mined campaign median for that tile
exhibits.expect_summary: tiles 701/703/704/706 placed as sprites

exhibits.label: SPRITE BRIDGE
exhibits.about: composing flat sprites into a solid volume you can walk across
exhibits.try: nothing yet: this is the technique we do not have, lettered where it would stand
exhibits.provenance: owner-named gap. Flat floor-aligned sprites composed into a walkable volume is a technique the pipeline cannot express

exhibits.label: REGISTER
exhibits.about: a counter with the working clearance behind it
exhibits.try: try to reach the working side from the front; the clearance is measured, not decorative
exhibits.provenance: reports/blood-assembly-counters.json, 384 mined bundles: waist-band rise 4096-8192, aspect at least 2, props on top, asymmetric access. E1M1 sector 80 is the worked example

exhibits.label: SHOP WINDOW
exhibits.about: a shopfront pane you can shoot out, with a display box behind it
exhibits.try: SHOOT the glass. kWallGib is the one mechanism in Blood that REOPENS a blocked wall -- the pane stops blocking, stops catching shots and stops being drawn, and you can step into the display. Everything else in the engine shuts things
exhibits.provenance: E6M1's shop front, read to the field: over_picnum 266 on a two-sided wall, cstat 0x00d5, XWALL trigger_vector with data 12. NBlood actor.cpp case 4 -> trTriggerWall kCmdWallImpact clears cstat 1|16|64 on BOTH sides. Promoted out of blood-city's glass.py
hand_composed: the display box: a room is a room, and the glass pass glazes the wall between it and the bay
exhibits.expect_summary: read as a a pane that can be shot out

exhibits.label: SHELF RUNS
exhibits.about: shelves as WALL TEXTURE on shallow sectors, in the three shop tiles
exhibits.try: a shelf is not a sprite: walk along and see them as geometry
exhibits.provenance: owner anchors 2026 and 2635, both strong binding, plus 202. E6M1's shop kit
exhibits.expect_summary: tiles 2026/2635 worn as wall texture, not thrown as sprites

exhibits.label: CRATE STACK
exhibits.about: crates as sector VOLUMES wearing the crate modules
exhibits.try: check these are crates, and that you can climb the small ones
exhibits.provenance: projects/blood-city/level/templates.py SMALL_CRATE (452, 1024 side, 16384 rise) and LARGE_CRATE (95, 2048, 32768). 459 is a moss-grown rock and a build once shipped it as a crate
hand_composed: the crate VOLUMES: the modules are imported from templates.py, but its _crate_block builds on the levelprog space stack, so the volumes themselves are assembled here on PlanarLayout
a free-standing crate in the middle of the floor is not expressible at all: PlanarLayout refuses a region wholly inside another, so these stand against a wall
exhibits.expect_summary: tiles 452/95 worn as wall texture, not thrown as sprites

exhibits.label: DISPLAY ROW
exhibits.about: three mannequins, standing on the floor they are seated to
exhibits.try: check they stand on the ground; in v1 they floated
exhibits.provenance: owner anchor 2377, binding strong. Its height is the one number here no campaign map backs: the tile has no mined median
exhibits.expect_summary: tiles 2377 placed as sprites

exhibits.label: FACADE NARROW
exhibits.about: a six-bay frontage with two openings and a sign
exhibits.try: stand back and read it; then compare it with the wide one
exhibits.provenance: reports/blood-facade-build.md: one wall tile across the run in 98% of 131 campaign multi-opening facades; bay 1024; reveal 256

exhibits.label: FACADE WIDE
exhibits.about: the same frontage at ten bays and three openings
exhibits.try: every relationship should survive the width change; only the counts differ
exhibits.provenance: reports/blood-facade-build.md width invariance: header, sill, reveal and sign seat are shared datums across both widths

exhibits.label: TURNSTILE PAIR
exhibits.about: two counter-rotating drums flanking a public way in
exhibits.try: walk into it. Whether a body passes a turning rotor is the pipeline's longest unproven claim
exhibits.provenance: reports/blood-turnstile-build.md; E1M4's carnival entry at period 255, four blades on tile 332, each spanning its rotor exactly
exhibits.expect_summary: 2 sector(s) of type 615

exhibits.label: TURNSTILE SAME WAY
exhibits.about: the same pair turning the same way, the DNE3L6 variant
exhibits.try: compare the two: counter-rotating is E1M4's, same-way is the community precedent
exhibits.provenance: reports/blood-turnstile-build.md; the community variant is precedent, never convention
exhibits.expect_summary: 2 sector(s) of type 615

exhibits.label: PIPE RUN
exhibits.about: a passage you duck along, four pipe tiles down it
exhibits.try: the clear height is deliberately below the campaign median; that is what a service run is
exhibits.provenance: reports/anchor-sewer-kit.json, role pipe_walls: tiles 496 to 499
hand_composed: the passage: four pipe sectors chained by hand, because no constructor owns a service run
exhibits.expect_summary: tiles 496/497/498/499 worn as wall texture, not thrown as sprites

exhibits.label: SEWER DOOR
exhibits.about: the technical door face, on a working z-motion door
exhibits.try: open it; the face is tile 500 and the mechanism is the same one the stone doors use
exhibits.provenance: reports/anchor-sewer-kit.json role sewer_door: tile 500. The mechanism is doors.z_motion_door
exhibits.expect_summary: 1 sector(s) of type 600, worked by a push

exhibits.label: SLIDING GATE
exhibits.about: two leaves parting into the jambs, serving the passage
exhibits.try: press it and watch where the leaves go; they rest shut and are drawn open
exhibits.provenance: mechanism.sliding_gate. A gate is authored in its OPEN pose and rests shut, which is what both campaign two-leaf gates do
exhibits.expect_summary: 1 sector(s) of type 614, listening on channel 302

exhibits.label: GROUND
exhibits.about: grass and dirt, the two-tile ground vocabulary
exhibits.try: the seam between them is where a path would go
exhibits.provenance: owner anchor 361 (grass, strong: dominant floor of E1M1's open-sky sectors, 35 of 66 uses under sky) with 270 dirt
hand_composed: ground cover beyond two sectors: no constructor owns a path or a planted bed
exhibits.expect_summary: tiles 361/270 worn as wall texture, not thrown as sprites

exhibits.label: TREES
exhibits.about: the four tree kinds, each at its own campaign height
exhibits.try: an oak is 2.82 player heights and a pine is not; check they differ
exhibits.provenance: furniture.py growing things; every height is the mined campaign median for that tile
exhibits.expect_summary: tiles 541/542/543/547 placed as sprites

exhibits.label: STRAW
exhibits.about: a heap of straw, at the height the campaign draws it
exhibits.try: 0.97 player heights: a heap you walk round, not a scatter underfoot
exhibits.provenance: tile 515, owner-named in the zoo specification. Campaign median height 0.97; the anchor file grades it untested, so the name here is the owner's and not ours
exhibits.expect_summary: tiles 515 placed as sprites

exhibits.label: STRONG BINDING
exhibits.about: the tiles the owner graded strong: these may name what they depict
exhibits.try: read the names and correct any that are wrong
exhibits.provenance: knowledge/blood/design/owner-anchors-v1.json, binding strong. Weak and untested tiles never name -- that rule is executable in owner_anchors.may_name
